My work develops estimators for panel data models that relax functional-form assumptions on
unobserved heterogeneity, and applies them to questions about innovation and firm productivity.

## Job market paper {#jmp}

::: {.paper}
[Job Market Paper]{.tag .tag-jmp}

<p class="paper-title">Semiparametric Panel Data Models with Interactive Fixed Effects</p>
<p class="paper-authors">Emma Kate Henry</p>

<div class="paper-abstract">
Methods for estimation and inference in semiparametric panel data models with both correlated
random effects and interactive fixed effects are developed, combining a Mundlak-style projection
for the time-invariant heterogeneity with a local-linear filter for the time-varying component.
Augmenting the partially linear regression with cross-sectional averages yields a Robinson-style
estimator that requires no iteration, principal components, or knowledge of the number of
factors. Asymptotic properties are established under joint large-<em>N</em>, large-<em>T</em>
asymptotics and illustrated with an application to innovation activity.
</div>

<p class="paper-venue">Draft available on request — [email me](mailto:ekhenry@crimson.ua.edu?subject=Job%20market%20paper).</p>

## Research experience

::: {.paper}
<p class="paper-title">Faculty Research Scholar — University of Alabama</p>
<p class="paper-venue">2022 – 2023</p>
<div class="paper-abstract">
Built data analysis methods for Google advertising cost data at both aggregate and segmented
levels, and contributed to machine learning algorithms using high-frequency, GPS-enabled
imaging to identify urban blight.
</div>
:::

::: {.paper}
<p class="paper-title">Research Assistant — Owen Vocational Rehabilitation Services</p>
<p class="paper-venue">2018 – 2022</p>
<div class="paper-abstract">
Conducted healthcare cost analysis forecasting lifetime care expenses for individuals with
catastrophic injuries in litigation, and assisted in preparing expert witness testimony.
</div>
:::

::: {.paper}
<p class="paper-title">Research Assistant — University of St Andrews</p>
<p class="paper-venue">2020</p>
<div class="paper-abstract">
Developed agent-based models of economic policy coordination, examining fiscal, monetary,
macro-prudential, and trade policy effects, with a literature review comparing game-theoretic
and agent-based approaches to policy cooperation.
</div>
:::
